title: Copies and factors
lede: One shop, fifteen questions. §1.2, before polynomials.

questions.stem: You have 1 book. A friend gives you their copy. How many books do you have?

opts.d: One book and one more book is two books.
The books are added, not written side by side.

work.why: One book and one more.

questions.stem: Say there are `x` books on the shelf. A friend brings 5 more. How many books are on the shelf now?

opts.d: `5x` is five shelves' worth. Five more books is `x + 5`. With 4 books on the shelf, 5 more makes 9, not 20.
`x^5` is five books multiplied together. Five more books is `x + 5`.
The `x` books are still there.

work.why: Four books on the shelf and five more makes nine, not twenty.

aspects.body: `x` is the number of books, not the books themselves. Five more books is `x + 5`; five shelves' worth would be `5x`.
Put `x` = 4 in. Four books and five more is nine. `5x` would be twenty.

questions.stem: Which is larger, `2x` or `x + 2`?

opts.d: At `x` = 1, `2x` is 2 and `x + 2` is 3. At `x` = 5 the other way round.
At `x` = 5, `2x` is 10 and `x + 2` is 7.
At `x` = 5 they are 10 and 7.

work.why: Equal at `x` = 2, and apart either side of it.

aspects.body: They are equal at `x` = 2, where both come to 4. Below 2 the sum is bigger; above 2 the product is.

questions.stem: The shop has 2 shelves, and each one holds 3 books. How many books is that?

opts.d: Adding gives 5. Each of the 2 shelves holds 3 books, so it is 2 lots of 3.
That would be 3 shelves of 3. There are 2 shelves here.
The two numbers are not written side by side.

work.why: Two rows of three.

questions.stem: Now 3 shelves, with 3 books on each. How many books?

opts.d: Adding gives 6, which is 2 shelves of 3. There are 3 shelves here, each with 3.
That was 2 shelves of 3.
That is 4 shelves of 3.

work.why: Three rows of three.

questions.stem: This time the shop has `x` shelves, and each one holds `x` books. How many books are in the shop?

opts.d: That is 2 shelves' worth. There are `x` shelves, each holding `x`.
That is 2 shelves of `x` books. The number of shelves is `x`, not 2.
Nothing is being added here.

work.why: 2 × 2 = 4, 3 × 3 = 9, and `x` × `x` = `x^2`.

aspects.body: The same `x` is doing two jobs at once: how many shelves, and how many books on each. One number, two roles.
3 shelves of 3 was a block 3 across and 3 down, 9 books in it. `x` shelves of `x` is that same block with the side left unsaid.
4 shelves of 4 books is 16 books. Shelves times books-per-shelf leaves books, not shelves.
If every shelf held 3 books instead of `x`, the shop would have `3x` books. At 5 shelves that is 15, not 25.

questions.stem: Does `x * x` equal `2x` for every value of `x`?

opts.d: At `x` = 5, `x * x` is 25 and `2x` is 10. They agree only at `x` = 0 and `x` = 2.

work.why: At `x` = 5, 25 against 10.

aspects.body: They do match at `x` = 0 and `x` = 2, so a single lucky value proves nothing. At `x` = 3 they are 9 and 6, and at `x` = 10 they are 100 and 20.

questions.stem: Simplify `x^2 + x^2`

opts.d: The exponents were added. `x^2` twice is two of the same thing, the way `7 + 7` is `2*7`.
Both numbers moved. Only one of them moves in a step.
Two shelves were counted as one.

work.why: Two of the same thing, as `7 + 7` is `2*7`.

aspects.body: `x^2 + x^2` is 2 of them, the same way `7 + 7` is `2 * 7`. `x^2 + x^3` is not 2 of anything.
In `2x^2` the 2 in front counts how many there are. The 2 up top counts how many `x`s are multiplied. At `x` = 3 that is 2 lots of 9, so 18.

questions.stem: Simplify `x^2 * x^2`

opts.d: Copies were counted. `(x*x)(x*x)` is four `x`'s in a row.
Both numbers moved. Only one of them moves in a step.
Nothing was combined. `(x*x)(x*x)` is four factors.

work.why: `(x*x)(x*x)` — four `x`'s.

aspects.body: `(x*x)(x*x)` written out is four `x`'s in a row. Count them; there is no rule to remember.
`x^2 * x^3` is `(x*x)(x*x*x)`, five `x`s in a row, so `x^5`. Count the `x`s and you have the rule.

questions.stem: For all numbers `k`, `k + k + k + k + k` can be written as

opts.d: `k^5` is five `k`'s multiplied. This is five `k`'s added, which is `5k`.
Five copies of `k`, not `k` and 5.
Nothing here adds 1 to `k`.

work.why: Five copies added.

questions.stem: Which of these expressions is equivalent to `n * n * n` for all values of `n`?

opts.d: `3n` is three `n`'s added. This is three multiplied, which is `n^3`.
Nothing is added here.
Nothing is divided here.

work.why: Three `n`'s multiplied.

questions.stem: Simplify `x^2 + x^3`

opts.d: The exponents were added. At `x` = 2 this is 4 + 8 = 12, and `x^5` is 32.
`x^2` and `x^3` are not copies of one thing.
`x^2` and `x^3` are not copies of one thing.

work.why: At `x` = 2 that is 4 + 8 = 12, while `x^5` is 32.

aspects.body: `x^2` and `x^3` are different kinds of thing, so there is nothing to count. It is 2 apples and 3 oranges.
At `x` = 2 this is 4 + 8 = 12. `x^5` would be 32. They are not the same expression.

questions.stem: Simplify `2x^2 + 3x^2`

opts.d: The exponent moved too. Adding moves only the number in front.
Everything was multiplied. The sign is a plus.
The fronts were multiplied. Two and three of a thing is five of it.

questions.stem: Simplify `2x^2 * 3x^2`

opts.d: The front is right; the exponent has not moved. There are four `x`'s here.
The fronts were added. In a product they multiply.
The whole thing was treated as a sum. The sign is a times.

work.why: In front, 2 times 3. Above, 2 plus 2.

aspects.body: `2x^2 * 3x^2`: the 2 and the 3 multiply to 6, and the two `x`'s and two more `x`'s make four, so `6x^4`.
`2x^2` is 2 tiles, each `x` by `x`. `3x^2` is 3 of the same tile. The 2 and the 3 multiply to 6; the `x`s multiply to `x^4`.

questions.stem: Simplify `x * x^2`

opts.d: A lone `x` is `x^1`, so it brings one factor: `x*x*x`.
Copies were counted. This is a product.
No count appears in front of a product of powers.

work.why: A lone `x` is `x^1`.

questions.stem: Put `x` = 2 into both sides of `2x^2 + 2x^2` = `4x^2`. Does it hold up?

opts.d: Both sides equal 16, so it holds.
`2x^2` at `x` = 2 is 2 times 4, which is 8.
`4x^2` at `x` = 2 is 4 times 4, which is 16.

work.why: The sides agree, so it holds.

aspects.body: Put `x` = 2 into `x^2 + x^2 = x^4` and you get 4 + 4 = 8 against 16. The sides disagree, so the rewriting is wrong.
Try it on `4^0 - 4^-1` or `(-4)^(3/2)`. When an exponent rule looks doubtful, put a number in before trusting it.

work.why: Two factors there, three more to reach five.

questions.stem: A press prints a book. Which of these changes when it prints one more copy?

opts.t: The paper and ink for that copy

opts.d: The rent is the same whether the press prints 1 copy or 1,000.

opts.t: The price printed on the cover
opts.d: The price is set in advance; printing one more does not change it.
Paper and ink are bought per copy.

work.why: What changes with the count is what carries an `x`.

aspects.body: Paper and ink carry an `x` because they are bought per copy: `7x`. The 4,000 does not, because it is the same at 1 copy and at 1,000.
`C = 7x + 4000` splits the same way every cost in this course does: `7x` moves with the count, 4,000 does not.

questions.stem: The press sells each copy for $18. Call the money coming in `R`. If it sells `x` copies, what is `R`?

opts.d: Each copy brings in 18 dollars, so `x` copies bring in `18x`.
That is one copy's worth. The press sells `x` of them.
That counts the copies, not the money.

work.why: A price for each one, times how many.

aspects.body: 18 is dollars for each copy, and there are `x` copies, so `18x` is dollars. At 500 copies that is 9,000 dollars.
500 copies bring in 9,000 dollars; 1,000 copies bring in 18,000. Double the copies, double the money.
Sell nothing and `R` = 18 × 0 = 0. Nothing printed, nothing taken in.

questions.stem: Printing costs $7 a copy, and the rent is $4,000 no matter how many copies are printed. Call the money going out `C`. What is `C`?

opts.d: This adds the 7 and the 4,000 as if both were charged per copy. The rent is $4,000 whether the press prints one copy or a thousand.
The rent still has to be paid.
The rent is paid once, not once per copy.

work.why: Costs come in pieces, and the pieces add.

aspects.body: At 1,000 copies `C` is 11,000, and 4,000 of that was owed before a single copy was printed. The two terms are the same units but not the same kind of cost.
At 500 copies, `C` is 3,500 + 4,000 = 7,500. The 3,500 moved with the count and the 4,000 did not.

questions.stem: Profit is whatever is left once the costs are paid. Call it `P`. Write `P` using `R` and `C`.

opts.d: This adds what the press spent to what it earned.
The wrong way round — this takes the earnings away from the costs.
Nothing here is being multiplied.

work.why: Written once with names, it holds whatever `R` and `C` turn out to be.

aspects.body: `R` is not a fixed number. Print 500 copies and `R` is 9,000; print 1,000 and `R` is 18,000. The letter names the amount, and the amount moves with `x`.
Once `P = R - C` becomes `11x - 4000`, the two steps collapse into one. At 500 copies you go straight to `11(500) - 4000` = 1,500, without working out 9,000 and 7,500 first.
`R` and `C` can never be negative — you cannot take in less than nothing or spend less than nothing. `P` can. At 250 copies `P` is -1,250.
`C - R` gives the same size with the opposite sign: 6,000 instead of -6,000 at 250 copies. It answers how far short the press fell, rather than what it made.
Writing `R = 18x` is already the idea behind `f(x) = 18x`: name the rule once, then feed it any `x`.

questions.stem: So `R = 18x` and `C = 7x + 4000`. Put those into `P = R - C`.

opts.d: `C` is the whole of `7x + 4000`, so all of it has to come off. Written this way the rent gets added on instead.
This adds everything the press spent to everything it earned.
That is `C - R`, the wrong way round.

work.why: `C` is a bundle, and the whole bundle comes off.

questions.stem: Selling 250 copies, the press really loses $1,250. Work out `18x - 7x + 4000` at 250 copies. What does it give?

opts.d: That is the true answer, but not what this expression gives. Try it: 4,500 − 1,750 + 4,000.
That is `11x` at 250, before the rent has been dealt with at all.
4,500 − 1,750 is 2,750, and this version then adds 4,000.

work.why: The truth is a $1,250 loss. Adding the rent instead of taking it off moved the answer by $8,000 — twice the rent.

questions.stem: Write `18x - (7x + 4000)` as a single expression.

opts.d: The minus has to reach the rent as well. Taking away `7x + 4000` takes away the 4,000 too.
The `7x` is being taken away, not added.
The rent has gone missing. It is still owed.

work.why: $11 left on each copy, and $4,000 to make up first.

aspects.body: `18x - (7x + 4000)` is `18x - 7x - 4000`. The minus reaches the 4,000 as well as the `7x`.
`18x` and `7x` combine because they count the same thing. The 4,000 has nothing to pair with, so it stays as it is.
Leave the parentheses out and the rent gets added instead. At 250 copies that reads $6,750 rather than a $1,250 loss — out by $8,000, twice the rent.
`(8x^2 - 7x + 27) - (3x^2 + 9x - 85)` is the same step: the minus reaches all three terms.

opts.t: The press starts $4,000 behind before it sells anything.
The press loses $4,000 on every copy.
opts.d: That would be `4000x`. The rent is charged once.
That is a different question, and the answer is not 4,000.
Each copy leaves 11 dollars. That is the other number.

questions.stem: A second book sells at $32 a copy, so `R = 32x`. Its costs work out to `C = 2x^2 + 12x + 5000`. Write `P = R - C` with those put in.

opts.d: All of `C` is being taken away, so all three of its terms sit inside the parentheses.
That is `C - R`, the wrong way round.
The costs are taken away, not added.

work.why: `C` is all three terms, so all three go inside.

aspects.body: `C` is a name for three terms at once. The parentheses are what hold them together while the minus acts on them.

questions.stem: Take the parentheses off `32x - (2x^2 + 12x + 5000)`.

opts.d: Only the first term changed sign. The minus reaches all three.
Every sign inside flips, and none of them stayed.
The 5,000 is inside too, so it is taken away as well.

work.why: The minus reaches all three terms.

aspects.body: Taking away a bundle takes away every part of it, so all three signs inside flip.
At `x` = 100 the costs are 20,000 + 1,200 + 5,000 = 26,200. Miss the 5,000 and the profit comes out 5,000 too high.

questions.stem: In `32x - 2x^2 - 12x - 5000`, which terms can be combined?

opts.d: One counts `x` squared and the other counts `x`. They are different kinds of term.
One carries an `x` and the other does not.
Only terms with the same power of `x` can be counted together.

work.why: Same power of `x`, so they count the same thing. The other two have no partner.

opts.d: `32x` and `-12x` make `20x`, not `44x`.
